title: Review: Polysaccharides; Lipids: triglycerides; Phospholipids, steroids and other lipids; Cardiovascular disease and risk

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Glycogen
items.clue: The energy store found in animals and fungi

items.label: Hydrophilic
items.clue: Describes the charged phosphate head, which interacts with water

items.label: Unsaturated
items.clue: Having at least one C=C double bond, which puts a kink in the hydrocarbon chain

items.label: Glucose
items.clue: The sugar monomer from which three different polysaccharides are built by condensation

questions.stem: Liver cells store glucose in the form of glycogen. Why is the glucose not simply stored as free glucose?

options.text: Glycogen is insoluble because it is non-polar, so it stays separate from the watery cytoplasm
The branches of glycogen make its glucose hard to remove, so the store is not used up too quickly
Glycogen is relatively insoluble because of its size, so it does not affect the osmotic balance of the cell
Glycogen stores extra energy in the glycosidic bonds that link its glucose monomers together

questions.explanation: Glycogen is very large and relatively insoluble, so much can be stored without raising the solute concentration of the cytoplasm. Free glucose would draw water in by osmosis.

questions.stem: To make a spread, manufacturers react a liquid vegetable oil with hydrogen, using a catalyst. Some C=C double bonds in its fatty acid chains become C–C single bonds. How does the oil change?

options.text: It becomes more liquid, as double bonds stiffen chains and hold molecules together.
It becomes more unsaturated, as it now carries more hydrogen atoms.
It becomes more solid, as straighter chains pack more closely together.
It becomes more solid, as the extra bonds need more heat to break when it melts.

questions.explanation: Fewer kinks, closer packing, stronger attractions between molecules: a higher melting point. A liquid oil becomes a soft solid, like butter in the hook.

questions.stem: Lipoproteins carry cholesterol and triglycerides in blood plasma, which is mostly water. Each lipoprotein has an oily core of cholesterol and triglyceride, surrounded by a single layer of phospholipids (with some proteins). How are the phospholipids in this layer most likely arranged?

options.text: Tails facing outwards into the plasma; heads facing inwards into the oily core.
Heads facing outwards into the plasma; tails pointing inwards into the oily core.
Tails joined to one another by covalent bonds, forming a rigid shell around the core.
Mixed evenly through the oily core, as phospholipids are entirely hydrophobic like cholesterol.

questions.stem: A person replaces butter with sunflower oil, keeping total fat intake the same. Why is this expected to lower their risk of cardiovascular disease?

options.text: Fat of any kind is harmful, so the benefit comes simply from eating less fat overall in the diet.
Unsaturated oils are liquid, so they cannot coat the inside of artery walls the way solid fats do.
Saturated fats are full of double bonds, which break apart in the blood and form plaques.
Swapping saturated for unsaturated fat lowers blood LDL, so less cholesterol enters artery walls.

questions.explanation: Lower LDL means less cholesterol enters damaged artery walls, so atheroma forms more slowly.

questions.stem: Humans make amylase, which hydrolyses the 1,4-glycosidic bonds between α-glucose units in starch. Humans make no enzyme that hydrolyses cellulose, which also has 1,4-glycosidic bonds between glucose units. Which explanation is best?

options.text: Cellulose's glycosidic bonds are much stronger than those in starch, so amylase cannot break them.
Cellulose chains are coiled and branched, so amylase cannot reach the bonds.
Cellulose is non-polar, so it cannot dissolve and enzymes cannot act on it.
Its β-glucose units alternate in orientation, so its bonds have a different shape.

questions.explanation: Amylase only fits bonds between α-glucose units. In cellulose, alternate β-glucose units are flipped, so the bond looks different to an enzyme. Cows rely on gut microbes that make cellulase.

questions.stem: One glycerol molecule and three fatty acid molecules react by condensation to form one triglyceride. How much water is produced?

options.text: One water molecule is released
Three water molecules are released
Four water molecules are released
No water is released; water is used up

questions.explanation: Each –OH of glycerol reacts with the carboxyl group of one fatty acid in a separate condensation, forming an ester bond and releasing one water: three in total.

questions.stem: Which components are linked together by condensation reactions to form one phospholipid molecule?

options.text: One glycerol, two fatty acids and one phosphate group
One glycerol, three fatty acids and one phosphate group
Three glycerol molecules, one fatty acid and one phosphate group
Many fatty acid monomers joined in a chain, plus one phosphate group

questions.explanation: Glycerol has three hydroxyl groups. In a phospholipid two of them are linked by condensation to fatty acids and the third to a phosphate group, giving two hydrophobic tails and a hydrophilic head.

questions.stem: Cellulose gives plant cell walls high tensile strength. Which feature of cellulose is responsible for this?

options.text: Straight chains lie side by side in bundles, cross-linked by many hydrogen bonds
The glycosidic bonds within cellulose are very much stronger than those within starch
The chains coil into tight helices that stretch and recoil like a spring
Beta-glucose is a larger monomer than alpha-glucose, giving thicker chains

questions.explanation: Straight, unbranched chains of β-glucose pack side by side in bundles linked by very many hydrogen bonds. Each is weak; together they resist stretching.

questions.stem: Phospholipids are shaken with water in a test tube, with no cells or enzymes present. What happens, and why?

options.text: Nothing organised forms, because phospholipid bilayers can only be built by enzymes inside living cells
Bilayers form, because covalent bonds link the fatty acid tails of neighbouring phospholipids
The phospholipids react with the water, because being amphipathic means acting as both an acid and a base
Bilayers form, because the hydrophilic heads face the water and the hydrophobic tails face each other

questions.explanation: The heads associate with water while the tails are excluded from it, so the molecules arrange themselves in a double layer, heads outwards and tails inwards. No enzymes are needed.
